title: Cyclotron
short_intro: A cyclotron is a compact particle accelerator that uses a constant magnetic field and a high-frequency alternating electric field to accelerate charged particles to high energies. Particles move in expanding spiral paths within two hollow, D-shaped metallic electrodes called dees.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Working principle, resonance condition, maximum kinetic energy formula, and frequency independence of the cyclotron for non-relativistic particles.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Relativistic mass variation effects, phase stability, high-frequency modifications (synchro-cyclotron), and particle beam focusing mechanisms.

prerequisites: Lorentz magnetic force on a moving charge (F = q(v × B))
Centripetal force mechanics in uniform circular motion
Alternating current circuits and resonance phenomena

concept_notes.heading: Construction and Basic Components
bullets: Consists of two hollow, semi-circular metal chambers called dees (D1 and D2) connected to a high-frequency alternating potential difference.
Placed inside an evacuated chamber between the pole pieces of a massive electromagnet that provides a uniform, perpendicular magnetic field.
A charged particle source is located at the exact center in the narrow gap between the two dees.

concept_notes.heading: Working Principle
bullets: A charged particle injected into the gap experiences an electric field and is accelerated into one of the dees.
Inside the dee, the electric field is zero (shielding effect), and the uniform magnetic field forces the particle to travel in a semi-circular path.

The frequency of the alternating electric field is synchronized with the revolution frequency of the particle so that the electric field reverses polarity precisely when the particle crosses the gap, ensuring continuous acceleration.

concept_notes.heading: Resonance Condition
bullets: For efficient acceleration, the frequency of the alternating applied voltage must exactly match the cyclotron frequency of the charged particle.
The time taken to complete a semi-circular path inside a dee is independent of the speed and radius of the particle trajectory.
This independence allows a constant oscillator frequency to be used for non-relativistic particles throughout their acceleration cycle.

concept_notes.heading: Limitations of a Conventional Cyclotron
bullets: At very high velocities (relativistic speeds), the relativistic mass of the particle increases, causing a decrease in its revolution frequency.
As a result, the particle falls out of step (synchronism) with the alternating electric field.

Consequently, conventional cyclotrons are unsuitable for accelerating electrons (due to their small mass and rapid onset of relativistic effects) or protons to very high (GeV) energies without modification.

derivations.title: Cyclotron Frequency and Time Period
derivations.conditions: Non-relativistic charged particle moving in a uniform perpendicular magnetic field
steps: Equate the magnetic Lorentz force to the required centripetal force: qvB = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}
Solve for the radius of the circular path: r = \frac{mv}{qB}
Express the angular frequency as omega = \frac{v}{r} = \frac{qB}{m}, and the frequency as f = \frac{omega}{2pi} = \frac{qB}{2pi m}

derivations.title: Maximum Kinetic Energy of Accelerated Particles
derivations.conditions: Particle exits the cyclotron at the maximum possible radius r = R (radius of the dees)
steps: From the radius formula r = \frac{mv}{qB}, express the maximum velocity v_{max} at r = R as v_{max} = \frac{qBR}{m}
Substitute v_{max} into the kinetic energy formula K_{max} = \frac{1}{2}mv_{max}^{2}

graphs_and_experiments.title: Spiral Trajectory of Particles in a Cyclotron
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Two semicircular dees with a gap in between, showing a spiral path starting from the center and expanding outward toward the edge.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Illustrates that as velocity increases due to gap acceleration, the radius of curvature increases proportionally, resulting in a widening spiral.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Frequently asked in conceptual questions regarding path geometry and radius scaling.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Kinetic Energy vs. Radius Squared
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A linear graph plotting K_{max} on the y-axis against R^{2} on the x-axis, passing through the origin.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Demonstrates the quadratic dependence of maximum kinetic energy on the dee radius (K propto R^{2}).
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used in numerical data interpretation and proportionality analysis.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Frequency vs. Energy (Relativistic Deviation)
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A horizontal straight line representing constant frequency in non-relativistic theory, and a downward curving line showing frequency dropping at high energies for relativistic particles.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Highlights why conventional cyclotrons fail for high-energy electrons or protons due to loss of resonance caused by mass increase.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: PGT-level conceptual testing on limitations and synchro-cyclotron corrections.

solved_numericals.question: A cyclotron is operating with a magnetic field of 1.5 T to accelerate protons (mass = 1.67 \times 10^{-27} kg, charge = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} C). Calculate the frequency of the alternating electric field required.
solution_steps: Identify given values: B = 1.5 T, q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} C, m = 1.67 \times 10^{-27} kg.
Use the cyclotron frequency formula: f = \frac{qB}{2pi m}.
Calculate result: f approx 2.28 \times 10^{7} Hz = 22.8 MHz.

solved_numericals.question: Find the maximum kinetic energy (in MeV) of deuterons accelerated by a cyclotron with a dee radius of 0.5 m and a magnetic field of 1.2 T. (Mass of deuteron = 3.34 \times 10^{-27} kg, charge = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} C).
solution_steps: Identify given parameters: B = 1.2 T, R = 0.5 m, q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} C, m = 3.34 \times 10^{-27} kg.
Use the maximum kinetic energy formula: K_{max} = \frac{q^{2}B^{2}R^{2}}{2m}.
Convert to MeV by dividing by 1.6 \times 10^{-13}: K_{max} = \frac{1.38 \times 10^{-12}}{1.6 \times 10^{-13}} approx 8.62 MeV.

solved_numericals.question: If the magnetic field in a cyclotron is doubled, what happens to the cyclotron frequency of a proton?
solution_steps: Recall the formula for cyclotron frequency: f = \frac{qB}{2pi m}.
Note that frequency is directly proportional to the magnetic field B (f propto B), assuming mass and charge remain constant.
When B is doubled, the frequency f must also double.

assumptions_and_limitations: Assumption: The magnetic field is perfectly uniform over the entire region of particle motion, which is difficult to maintain at the edges.
Limitation: Relativistic mass increase at high velocities causes the particle to lag behind the electric field, restricting conventional cyclotron energy limits.
Limitation: Cyclotrons cannot accelerate neutral particles (neutrons) or uncharged bodies because magnetic and electric forces act only on moving charges.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The electric field inside the dees accelerates the charged particles.
common_misconceptions.correct: The electric field inside the dees is zero; acceleration occurs exclusively in the gap between the dees.
common_misconceptions.why: A hollow conductor shields its interior from external electrostatic fields.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The time period of revolution depends on the speed and radius of the particle.
common_misconceptions.correct: The time period of a non-relativistic particle in a cyclotron is independent of its speed and radius.
common_misconceptions.why: As speed increases, the radius increases proportionally, keeping the time taken for a semi-circular orbit constant (T = \frac{pi m}{qB}).

common_misconceptions.wrong: Cyclotrons can accelerate electrons to very high speeds easily.
common_misconceptions.correct: Cyclotrons are inefficient for accelerating electrons to high energies.
common_misconceptions.why: Electrons have a very small rest mass, causing them to reach relativistic speeds rapidly and lose synchronization with the oscillator frequency.

quick_revision: Cyclotron frequency depends only on the specific charge (q/m) and magnetic field B, independent of radius and speed for non-relativistic particles.
